verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The train slows for a station no one gets off at.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Rain on the window keeps its own schedule,
tracing the names of towns we won't stop in.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A conductor checks a watch that isn't broken,
just tired of counting minutes no one claims.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone folds a timetable into a paper boat,
sets it adrift on the aisle's thin river of dust.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The boat runs aground on a stranger's shoe,
who lifts his foot, apologizing to no one,
and lets the small vessel sail on.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The paper boat noses past a sleeping child's shoelace,
still charting a course toward whatever port it imagines.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Somewhere past the child's dream a harbor waits,
built from the folds of every timetable
that ever learned to float instead of arrive.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The harbor has no clocks, only the tide's slow arithmetic,
and every folded ship is finally, quietly, on time.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The tide subtracts nothing, only gathers—
each paper hull returning to blank sheet,
ready for someone else's hand to fold.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else's hand, chapped from waking early,
finds the sheet still damp with harbor water
and folds it anyway, not knowing what it makes.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
It becomes a bird, or a boat, or nothing—
the hand doesn't wait to see,
already reaching for the next wet page.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The next page never blames the hand for leaving—
it just soaks up whatever light is left
and waits its turn to become something.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Waiting its turn, it learns the patience of paper—
how light itself will fold and unfold again,
never asking to be more than what arrives.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
What arrives is enough: a name half-written,
the ink already deciding for itself
where the water wants the word to end.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Where the word ends, someone else begins it—
a stranger's hand completing the loose stroke,
as if all ink remembers whose turn is next.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Whose turn is next, the doorstep doesn't wonder—
it just wears thin beneath each different shoe,
learning the weight of feet it never chose.
